meta.source: OrcaSlicer wiki, Obico calibration guide, general FDM troubleshooting community knowledge
meta.notes: Printer-agnostic general troubleshooting guide. Covers common print quality issues, filament issues, and OrcaSlicer-specific tips. Intended to complement the printer-specific HMS and maintenance databases.

issues.name: Stringing / hairy prints
issues.summary: Thin threads of filament between separate parts of the print.
symptoms: Hair-like threads between pillars or separate sections
Cobweb appearance on prints with multiple towers
Blobs where the nozzle restarts after a travel move
likely_causes: Nozzle temperature too high, lowering filament viscosity and encouraging ooze
Retraction distance or speed insufficient for the extruder type
Travel speed too slow, allowing more time for ooze
Combing/avoid-crossing-perimeters disabled
Wet or degraded filament
fix_steps: Reduce nozzle temperature by 5°C increments and test. Start at the lower end of the filament's recommended range.
For direct drive printers (Bambu, Voron): retraction 0.4-1.0mm at 30-45mm/s.
For Bowden printers (Ender 3, etc.): retraction 4-7mm at 40-60mm/s.
Enable 'Combing' or 'Avoid crossing perimeters' in Process > Travel to minimize open-air travels.
Increase travel speed so the nozzle crosses gaps faster.
Dry your filament if stringing is sudden or much worse than before.
Enable Z-hop paired with retraction to lift the nozzle above printed areas during travel.
Run OrcaSlicer's retraction calibration from the Calibration menu.

issues.name: Print not sticking to the bed
issues.summary: First layer does not adhere, or print detaches during printing.
symptoms: First layer peels up or slides while printing
Print detaches mid-print
First layer visually appears to not be pressed onto the bed
Corners lift during printing
likely_causes: Dirty build plate with oils or residue reducing adhesion
Z offset too high, leaving a gap between nozzle and bed
Bed temperature too low for the material
Incorrect build plate type for the material
First layer speed too fast
fix_steps: Clean the build plate thoroughly with IPA (isopropyl alcohol 90%+) and a clean paper towel.
Do not touch the cleaned surface with bare hands.
Check and adjust Z offset: the first layer should be slightly squished, not floating.
Increase bed temperature: PLA 55-65°C, PETG 70-85°C, ABS/ASA 90-110°C.
Reduce first layer print speed to 20-30mm/s.
Use the correct plate for the material: smooth PEI for PLA, textured PEI for PETG, engineering plate for ABS/Nylon.
Add a brim in OrcaSlicer for models with small footprints.
Run a bed leveling/mesh calibration.

issues.name: Warping / corners lifting
issues.summary: Print corners or edges curl up off the bed during or after printing.
symptoms: Corners of the print visibly lifting off the bed
Print detaches during printing specifically at edges
Completed print is curved or bowed on the bottom
likely_causes: Material-specific thermal contraction (especially ABS, ASA, Nylon, PC)
Insufficient bed temperature
Ambient temperature too cold or drafts cooling the print
No enclosure for high-warp materials
Cooling fan too aggressive on early layers
fix_steps: Use an enclosure (or close the P1S door) for ABS, ASA, Nylon, and PC.
Increase bed temperature to the upper end of the material's range.
Turn off or reduce the part cooling fan for the first 3-5 layers.
Add a brim of 5-10mm width to anchor the perimeter to the bed.
Apply a thin layer of PVA glue stick to the build plate for additional grip.
Avoid placing very large flat prints near the edges of the bed.
Reduce print speed for perimeters to allow better layer bonding.

issues.name: Under-extrusion / gaps in walls
issues.summary: Printer is not extruding enough filament, causing gaps, weak layers, or missing sections.
symptoms: Gaps between perimeter walls or infill
Layers look thin or incomplete
Extruder motor makes clicking sounds
Weak or brittle prints that break easily
likely_causes: Partial or full nozzle clog
Nozzle temperature too low for the filament
Print speed exceeding the hotend's maximum volumetric flow rate
Filament grinding from extruder gear (filament surface stripped)
Filament diameter inconsistency or wet filament
Flow ratio calibrated too low
fix_steps: Check for a clog: heat the nozzle and manually push filament through. Resistance or no flow indicates a clog.
Perform a cold pull to clear partial blockage.
Increase nozzle temperature by 5-10°C.
Reduce print speed, starting with infill and perimeter speeds.
Clean the extruder gear of filament dust buildup.
Run OrcaSlicer's Max Volumetric Speed calibration to find your actual limit.
Run flow calibration and adjust flow ratio in the filament profile.
Dry the filament if all else fails.

issues.name: Over-extrusion / blobs and rough surfaces
issues.summary: Printer is extruding too much filament, causing blobs, rough surfaces, and dimensional inaccuracy.
symptoms: Rough or bumpy outer surface
Blobs or zits on the surface
Parts are dimensionally larger than expected
Layers not bonding properly due to excessive material
likely_causes: Flow ratio set too high
Nozzle temperature too high causing excessive ooze
E-steps or rotation distance miscalibrated in firmware
Filament diameter in profile does not match actual filament
fix_steps: Run OrcaSlicer's flow calibration from the Calibration menu.
Reduce flow ratio in the filament profile by 2-5% increments and test.
Reduce nozzle temperature slightly.
Measure your filament diameter with calipers at several points and update the filament profile if it differs from 1.75mm.
Check that pressure advance (PA) is calibrated; uncalibrated PA can cause corner blobs.

issues.name: Layer shifting
issues.summary: Layers are offset from each other, causing a staircase or leaning appearance.
symptoms: Print suddenly shifts to one side partway up
Staircase pattern on print walls
Print looks like it leaned during printing
likely_causes: Belt too loose on X or Y axis
Print speed or acceleration too high
Obstruction in the motion path (fallen parts, clips, cable snag)
Stepper motor driver overheating
External vibration from the surface the printer is on
fix_steps: Check belt tension on both X and Y axes. Pluck the belt; it should have a consistent, firm tone.
Check for any physical obstruction: fallen parts, cable snag, clips on the motion path.
Reduce print speed and acceleration in Process > Speed.
Run vibration compensation calibration on the printer.
Place the printer on a stable, level surface away from vibration sources.
Check that the printer has adequate cooling and ventilation around the electronics.

issues.name: Layer delamination / poor layer adhesion
issues.summary: Layers separate or crack apart, especially on tall or stressed prints.
symptoms: Layers visibly separating on the finished print
Print cracks easily along layer lines when bent
Horizontal cracks visible on tall prints
likely_causes: Nozzle temperature too low for adequate layer bonding
Layer height too large relative to the line width
Print speed too fast, not allowing proper bonding time
Cooling too aggressive, cooling layers before the next layer bonds
Wet or degraded filament
fix_steps: Increase nozzle temperature by 5-10°C.
Reduce layer height (as a rule, no more than 75% of nozzle diameter).
Reduce print speed, especially for perimeters.
Reduce cooling fan speed or add minimum layer time to slow cooling.
Dry the filament before printing.
For PETG specifically: reduce cooling fan below 50% to improve layer bonding.

issues.name: Ringing / ghosting on print walls
issues.summary: Ripple or wave patterns on print walls, especially after corners or sharp direction changes.
symptoms: Wavy ripple pattern on outer walls near corners
Ghosting of sharp features appearing downstream on the wall
likely_causes: Print speed or acceleration too high causing resonance
Belt tension too low
Printer placed on an unstable or vibrating surface
Loose toolhead or mechanical play
fix_steps: Run vibration compensation (resonance) calibration on the printer.
Reduce outer wall print speed.
Check belt tension on X and Y axes.
Place the printer on a stable, rigid surface. Anti-vibration feet can help.
In OrcaSlicer, enable or tune Pressure Advance to reduce corner blobs that can amplify ringing.
If using Klipper: tune input shaping with an ADXL345 accelerometer.

issues.name: Elephant's foot (first layer too wide)
issues.summary: The first few layers are wider than the rest of the print, creating a flared base.
symptoms: Base of print is wider than the model
First layers visibly bulge outward
Tight-tolerance parts do not fit because the base is oversized
likely_causes: Z offset too low, squishing the first layer excessively
First layer flow ratio too high
Bed temperature too high for the material (especially PLA)
fix_steps: Increase Z offset slightly (raise the nozzle) so the first layer is less squished.
Reduce first layer flow ratio in Process > Quality (try 95%).
Reduce bed temperature by 5°C.
The first layer should be slightly squished for adhesion but not flattened excessively.
Use OrcaSlicer's Elephant Foot Compensation setting in Process > Others.

issues.name: Wet / moisture-absorbed filament
issues.summary: Filament has absorbed moisture from the air, causing print quality issues.
symptoms: Popping, crackling, or hissing sounds during printing
Rough, bubbly, or foamy surface texture
Stringing suddenly much worse than usual
Steam or vapor visible from the nozzle area
Inconsistent extrusion and flow
likely_causes: Filament stored in open air without a sealed container or desiccant
High humidity environment
Spool opened and used over many months
fix_steps: Dry the filament in a filament dryer or food dehydrator at the appropriate temperature.
PLA: 45-55°C for 4-6 hours. PETG: 65°C for 4-6 hours. ABS/ASA: 70°C for 4-6 hours. Nylon: 80°C for 8-12 hours.
Do not use a standard kitchen oven unless it can hold low temperatures accurately.
Store filament in a sealed bag or container with fresh silica gel desiccant when not in use.
Consider a dry box or active dry storage solution for hygroscopic materials (Nylon, TPU, PVA).

issues.name: Full nozzle clog
issues.summary: No filament exits the nozzle despite the extruder running.
symptoms: No filament comes out during printing
Extruder motor clicks or skips consistently
Filament grinds away at the extruder gear
Manually pushing filament at temperature meets solid resistance
likely_causes: Carbonized filament blocking the nozzle orifice
Foreign debris in the hotend
Printing too cold allowing filament to solidify in the melt zone
Heat creep: filament softening and jamming in the cold zone above the heatbreak
fix_steps: Heat the nozzle to 20-30°C above the normal printing temperature and try to push filament through manually.
Perform multiple cold pulls with PLA to draw out the blockage.
Use an acupuncture needle or nozzle cleaning needle (0.3mm) to clear the orifice while at temperature.
If the clog is in the cold zone (heat creep): ensure the hotend fan is running and check for obstructions.
If cold pulls and needle cleaning fail, replace the nozzle.
After clearing, check the hotend fan is running during warm-up to prevent heat creep recurrence.

issues.name: Inconsistent extrusion / variable line width
issues.summary: Extrusion varies in width or thickness along a single perimeter or layer.
symptoms: Wall lines that vary in width or look bumpy
Inconsistent surface texture that changes mid-print
Pressure advance calibration patterns that vary between segments
likely_causes: Filament diameter inconsistency (measure with calipers at multiple points)
Partial clog creating intermittent resistance
Extruder gear slip or wear
PTFE tube damage causing friction in the filament path
fix_steps: Measure filament diameter at 5+ points with calipers. More than 0.05mm variation is significant.
Check the extruder gear for wear or packed filament dust.
Inspect the PTFE tube from extruder to nozzle for kinks or internal damage.
Perform a cold pull to check for partial blockage.
Try a different spool to rule out filament quality as the cause.

issues.name: Poor top surface quality
issues.summary: Top surfaces have ridges, gaps, bumps, or an uneven texture.
symptoms: Ridges or lines visible on flat top surfaces
Gaps between top layer lines
Pillowing: raised bumps or dimples on the top surface
likely_causes: Too few top solid layers (pillowing due to infill showing through)
Top surface speed too fast
Insufficient cooling causing top layers to sag
Under-extrusion on top layers
Ironing not enabled for surfaces that need it
fix_steps: Increase top solid layers to at least 4-5.
Reduce top surface speed in Process > Speed.
Increase cooling fan speed for top layers.
Enable ironing in Process > Quality for flat top surfaces.
If pillowing: increase infill density or add more top layers so infill does not show through.
Ensure flow is calibrated correctly.

issues.name: Supports hard to remove / fusing to model
issues.summary: Support structures are difficult to remove without damaging the model.
symptoms: Support breaks the model surface during removal
Support is bonded to the model and cannot be pulled away
Surface under the support is rough or marked after removal
likely_causes: Support Z distance too small or set to 0
No support interface layers configured
Support interface material same as model material (both bonding strongly)
fix_steps: Increase support top Z distance to 0.15-0.25mm in Process > Support.
Enable support interface layers (2-3 layers) to create a cleaner break surface.
Reduce support interface flow ratio to 90% for easier removal.
Use a different interface material if your printer supports multi-material (soluble PVA or HIPS).
For tree supports, they typically remove more easily than grid supports on organic shapes.
Score the support junction with a craft knife before pulling to reduce tearing.

issues.name: Print stuck to bed / won't release
issues.summary: Finished print is extremely difficult to remove from the build plate without damage.
symptoms: Print cannot be removed by normal flex and peel of the plate
Print surface is damaged when forcing removal
Build plate coating is damaged over time from stuck prints
likely_causes: Z offset too low causing excessive first layer squish and too much contact area
Bed temperature too high creating strong bond
Wrong plate for the material (PLA on textured PEI can over-stick)
Glue stick applied when not needed
fix_steps: Allow the bed to cool to below 35°C. Many materials release naturally as they contract on cooling.
Flex the flexible build plate away from the magnetic base to pop the print free.
Use a stiff plastic spatula at the edge to lever the print up; avoid metal scrapers that damage PEI.
Raise Z offset slightly for future prints to reduce squish.
For PLA on textured PEI: try letting the bed cool to room temperature before removal.
Do not apply glue stick to textured PEI for PLA unless specifically needed.

issues.name: How to calibrate Pressure Advance (PA)
issues.summary: Pressure Advance (also known as Linear Advance in Marlin) compensates for filament pressure lag, improving corner sharpness.
symptoms: Blobs or zits at corners and seams
Underextrusion at the start of lines after a travel
Over-extrusion at the end of lines before a travel or corner
likely_causes: Pressure advance not calibrated for the current filament and temperature
PA value from a different filament type applied incorrectly
fix_steps: In OrcaSlicer, go to Calibration > Pressure Advance.
Select your printer and filament and run the calibration print.
Inspect the resulting pattern: find the line where corners are sharpest without blobs.
Note the PA value shown on the pattern at that point.
Enter that value in Filament Settings > Filament > Pressure Advance.
PA is filament and temperature specific: recalibrate when changing materials or temperatures significantly.

issues.name: How to calibrate flow rate (extrusion multiplier)
issues.summary: Flow rate calibration ensures the slicer commands match the actual amount of filament being extruded.
symptoms: Prints consistently over- or under-sized
Surface quality poor despite other settings being correct
Gaps in top layers or overfilled infill
likely_causes: New filament spool with slightly different characteristics
Nozzle wear changing effective orifice size
Flow ratio never calibrated for this filament
fix_steps: In OrcaSlicer, go to Calibration > Flow Rate.
Print the calibration object and identify the segment with the smoothest surface.
Apply the recommended flow ratio change from that segment.
Confirm by printing a second calibration pass if the first result is not centered.
Save the corrected flow ratio in your filament profile.
Calibrate temperature first before flow rate, as temperature affects optimal flow.

issues.name: How to calibrate printing temperature
issues.summary: Find the optimal nozzle temperature for a specific filament using a temperature tower.
symptoms: Stringing that cannot be fixed by retraction alone
Poor layer adhesion or delamination
Overhangs melting or drooping
Matte or glossy surface finish inconsistencies
likely_causes: Using a temperature outside the optimal range for the specific filament brand and color
Temperature set to defaults without accounting for this filament
fix_steps: In OrcaSlicer, go to Calibration > Temperature.
Set a temperature range covering the filament's recommended range (e.g. 195-225°C for PLA).
Print the temperature tower.
Inspect each zone: look for the best combination of layer adhesion, surface finish, overhang quality, and minimal stringing.
Update the nozzle temperature in your filament profile to the optimal value found.
Temperature is filament-specific: different brands and even colors of the same brand can vary by 5-15°C.

issues.name: How to calibrate Z offset and first layer
issues.summary: Set the correct Z offset so the first layer is properly squished for adhesion without being too flat.
symptoms: First layer not sticking
Elephant's foot (first layer too wide)
Gaps in first layer where the nozzle is too far from the bed
Nozzle dragging through first layer
likely_causes: Z offset not calibrated after changing build plates
Bed leveling not run recently
Different plate thickness than what calibration was done with
fix_steps: Run bed leveling calibration from the printer settings.
Print a first layer calibration square or line.
The first layer should be slightly squished and fill in completely with no gaps, but not so squished that the lines are indistinguishable.
Adjust Z offset in small increments (0.05mm) and re-test.
On Bambu printers, Z offset is adjusted from the printer screen during or after the first layer.
Recalibrate after changing build plates, as different plates have different thicknesses.

issues.name: How to find maximum volumetric flow rate
issues.summary: Determine the maximum flow rate your hotend can sustain without under-extrusion.
symptoms: Under-extrusion at high speeds
Print quality degrades when using fast speed profiles
Unsure what the safe maximum speed is for your hotend and filament
likely_causes: Printing faster than the hotend can melt filament
No calibrated volumetric speed limit set in the filament profile
fix_steps: In OrcaSlicer, go to Calibration > Max Volumetric Speed.
Print the calibration object, which gradually increases flow rate.
Find the point where quality degrades (under-extrusion, layer gaps).
Set the Max Volumetric Speed in your filament profile to 80% of that found limit for a safety margin.
Typical values: Standard brass nozzle PLA 15-22mm³/s, PETG 10-18mm³/s. CHT high-flow nozzle: 25-40mm³/s.
For Bambu P1S: the stock hotend typically supports 18-24mm³/s depending on material.

issues.name: Printing abrasive filaments (CF, GF, Glow, Grit)
issues.summary: Tips for printing carbon fiber, glass fiber, glow-in-the-dark, and other abrasive materials.
fix_steps: Use a hardened steel nozzle. Brass nozzles will wear out significantly faster with abrasive materials.
Keep nozzle temperature at the higher end of the recommended range for the base material (PLA-CF: 220-240°C).
Reduce print speed compared to standard PLA by 20-30%.
Clean the extruder gear more frequently: every 1-2 spools instead of every 5.
Use a build plate that works with the base material (PLA-CF uses same plates as PLA).
Carbon fiber filaments are brittle: avoid sharp bends in the filament path and use a high-quality PTFE tube.
Dry carbon fiber filaments before use; they absorb moisture similarly to their base material.

issues.name: Setting up OrcaSlicer for a new printer
issues.summary: First steps for configuring OrcaSlicer correctly when adding a new printer.
fix_steps: Add your printer from the built-in profile list in File > Printer Management where possible.
Verify the bed size and shape match your physical printer in Printer Settings.
Check machine start and end G-code against what your printer firmware expects.
Run calibrations in order: Temperature first, then Flow Rate, then Pressure Advance, then Max Volumetric Speed.
Save calibrated results into named filament profiles for each filament you use.
Back up your profiles by exporting them from File > Export Configs.
For Klipper printers: add [exclude_object] and [gcode_arcs] to printer.cfg before using OrcaSlicer features that require them.
